title: LANE KIFFIN TEMPERATURE CHECK
dek: Eight ecosystem readings around the LSU merger before Game One, with Ole Miss still operating as the live counterargument.
body:
LSU did not hire Lane Kiffin to make football interesting. It hired him to convert Louisiana, capital, portal fluency, and Saturday night into a championship system—and to do it while his former program remains a live rebuttal.

The Lane Kiffin Temperature Check is PointCast Coaches Desk 003. Its 96-degree overall signal measures preseason pressure, attention, change, and unresolved public meaning. It is not a win projection, poll, hot-seat grade, employment evaluation, player-sentiment measure, betting product, or audited financial analysis. LSU has played zero 2026 games.

Eight rooms receive separate readings: Program, Players, Capital, Area, Staff, Press, Foes, and Fans. The football case begins with Kiffin's 55 wins in six Ole Miss seasons and a system that led the SEC in total offense four times. The new roster was reconstructed around a reported 40-player transfer haul led by quarterback Sam Leavitt, tackle Jordan Seaton, and edge Princewill Umanmielen. The operating room now includes a seven-year, $91 million coaching deal and what LSU calls an NFL-style front office managing roster, NIL, revenue share, strategy, and partnerships.

Louisiana is treated as a competitive system rather than backdrop. Elite in-state signees stayed through the transition, Ed Orgeron returned as a special assistant to recruiting and defense, and defensive coordinator Blake Baker supplies continuity as one of four retained defensive coaches.

The split screen remains Oxford. Ole Miss reached a national semifinal after Kiffin left, kept quarterback Trinidad Chambliss and running back Kewan Lacy, and signed the reported No. 2 portal class. LSU visits Ole Miss on September 19, two weeks after opening against Clemson. Texas A&M, Alabama, and Texas all visit Tiger Stadium later in the season.

The closing section asks what Paul Finebaum would probably say. It is clearly labeled PointCast synthesis—not a quote, transcript, endorsement, impersonation, or statement by Finebaum or ESPN. It is built from the documented tension between Finebaum's January criticism of Kiffin's departure optics and his July forecast that Kiffin will probably win a national title at LSU within two or three years.

Every current factual claim is paired with a public source. Primary LSU records establish appointment, roster, schedule, staff, and front-office structure. Associated Press and CBS reporting supply contract, portal, and Ole Miss aftermath context. Commentary remains labeled as commentary.
